verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the goal follows the custom rmgr pattern. Demand is the main open point: the fsync validation use case does not follow from dispatch by FileTag.handler (demand-1), which leaves Lamstore as the only consumer (demand-2). One design point also stands: handler IDs come from load order and no runtime check catches a mismatch between processes (replication-ondisk-1). Only the author has posted, so this rests on thin material.

brief.title: Extension API to register custom checkpoint sync handlers
brief.problem: Extensions cannot add entries to the checkpoint fsync dispatch table, because syncsw[] in sync.c is a fixed static array. The author's extent-based storage extension, Lamstore, keeps data at byte offsets inside a volume file, so it cannot reuse SYNC_HANDLER_MD, which fsyncs md segment paths. The author also cites fsync validation tools that Heikki Linnakangas and Andres Freund asked for in the CF 5616 thread.
brief.proposed_design: syncsw[] becomes a heap-allocated table that grows by repalloc. InitSyncHandlers() registers the five built-in handlers at their existing IDs 0 to 4 before shared_preload_libraries load; under EXEC_BACKEND, register_sync_handler() also calls it. Extensions call register_sync_handler() from _PG_init, get an int16 ID from SYNC_HANDLER_FIRST_DYNAMIC on, and put it in FileTag.handler.
user_visible_surface: New C function register_sync_handler(const SyncOps *ops, const char *name) returning int16; calls after preload raise FATAL.
SyncOps struct moves to the public header storage/sync.h.
SyncRequestHandler enum: new SYNC_HANDLER_FIRST_DYNAMIC = 5 and SYNC_HANDLER_MAX; SYNC_HANDLER_NONE changes from 5 to -1.
New documentation chapter custom-sync-handler.sgml, modeled on custom-rmgr.sgml.
New test module src/test/modules/test_sync_handler with a TAP test.
author_claims: The change is strictly additive, with no changes to WAL format, FileTag layout, shared memory or catalogs, and no behaviour change without a registered extension.
Per-dispatch assembly is byte identical to stock on GCC 14.2 -O2; the only cost is one extra load per ProcessSyncRequests call.
Commit 3eb77eba5a5 (PG12) planned for non-md sync handler users, so this patch adds the missing registration step.
The patch is independent of CF 5616 (extensible smgr) and composes with it.
v2 passes check-world on fork and EXEC_BACKEND builds, and CFbot is green on all platforms.
brief.thread_state: Only the author has posted: v1, a v2 that fixes EXEC_BACKEND registration order, and a status ping saying no review yet. A reviewer signed up in the CommitFest on 2026-11-09 but has not posted.
unclear: The material calls the patch ABI safe but also changes the SYNC_HANDLER_NONE value; it does not discuss impact on already compiled extensions.
The proposal does not say what happens to queued sync requests whose handler ID is unknown, for example after the extension is removed from shared_preload_libraries.
The proposal does not say whether any registered handler can see sync requests of other handlers, as the fsync validation use case claims.
There is no benchmark of checkpoint time, only an assembly comparison.
The proposal does not say how two extensions avoid clashing FileTag conventions or whether handler names must be unique.

objections.title: The fsync validation use case is not served by this design
objections.failure_scenario: A developer writes the fsync validation extension, registers a handler and gets ID 5. The checkpointer sends it only requests whose FileTag.handler is 5. Requests from md, CLOG and multixact still go to handlers 0 to 4, so the extension sees none of the missing-fsync cases it was built to find.
objections.argument: Message #1 counts the needs that Heikki Linnakangas and Andres Freund mentioned as demand and says a validation extension would "observe every sync request". The proposed dispatch is syncsw[idx], where idx comes from the requester's FileTag, so a registered handler gets only its own requests. The proposal adds no observer or hook on ProcessSyncRequests. Without that use case, the demand rests on one extension.
objections.author_must_show: How would a handler registered at ID 5 see sync requests that md.c and slru.c queue under IDs 0 to 4?

critic.reasoning: The proposal dispatches by FileTag.handler and adds no observer on ProcessSyncRequests, so a registered handler receives only its own requests. The claim in message #1 that a validation extension observes every sync request does not follow from the design.

objections.title: Demand rests on one unreleased extension from the author
objections.failure_scenario: Core adds a public SyncOps API and a documentation chapter for one consumer, Lamstore. Later changes to sync.c, such as a new built-in handler or a change to FileTag, must keep this API stable for extensions that may not exist. If Lamstore changes direction, core still carries the API.
objections.argument: The material names one consumer, the author's Lamstore, and gives no release, user count or production numbers. Only the author has posted in the thread, across three CommitFests (messages #1 to #3). The Percona branch note in message #1 points to the same deployment, so it is not independent demand. The benefit goes to extension authors, but the API surface and enum change apply to everyone.
objections.author_must_show: Which other extensions, table AMs or storage projects need checkpoint fsync of non-md files today, and how do they handle it now?

critic.reasoning: The material names Lamstore as the only working consumer, and only the author has posted across three CommitFests. The 2019 commit message mentions other proposed users, but the thread shows none today.

objections.title: Handler IDs from load order are not checked to match across processes
objections.failure_scenario: On an EXEC_BACKEND build such as Windows, one extension's _PG_init skips register_sync_handler() in some processes, for example based on process type or a GUC. A backend then queues a FileTag with handler 6, and the checkpointer resolves 6 to another extension's SyncOps or to nothing. Pages are reported synced but never fsynced, which shows up only as data loss after an OS crash.
objections.argument: Message #2 says each EXEC_BACKEND child re-runs shared_preload_libraries and assigns IDs again in its own address space. The design assumes every process reaches the same IDs, but nothing enforces it. The name argument to register_sync_handler() is not used to cross-check IDs, and the commit message lists only Asserts for bounds. The RegisterCustomRmgr parallel in message #1 does not cover this, because rmgr IDs are fixed constants chosen by the extension and are not assigned at runtime.
objections.author_must_show: What makes the checkpointer reject, rather than silently misroute, a FileTag whose handler ID maps to a different registered name, or to no name, in a non-Assert build?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 confirms each EXEC_BACKEND child assigns IDs again, and the commit message lists only Asserts as bounds checks. The trigger is an extension that registers conditionally, but the result is a silently skipped fsync, so a runtime check is a fair request.

refuted.title: Sync handler API fixed before the extensible smgr design settles
refuted.failure_scenario: Core ships register_sync_handler() in v20 while extensible smgr is still open. Later the smgr work picks a hook-based or per-tablespace design whose sync needs differ from a preload-time integer registry. Then core must keep two inconsistent extension APIs, or break the released one for extension authors.
refuted.argument: The main consumer in message #1 is a storage backend that routes I/O through a custom storage manager. Two earlier attempts at extensible smgr were returned, [P6] for inactivity and [P5] with redo and catalog problems. The [P5] summary says hook versus registration was still unsettled at the end. Message #1 says this patch avoids those questions, but that also means it fixes one answer for sync.c before the smgr answer exists.
refuted.author_must_show: If extensible smgr ends up hook-based or per-tablespace, does register_sync_handler() still fit without change, and which non-smgr user needs it today?

critic.reasoning: The scenario does not say how a hook-based or per-tablespace smgr would change sync dispatch, which core already indexes by FileTag.handler. [P6] closed for inactivity and [P5] for catalog and redo problems, neither of which touches sync.c.

refuted.title: Fsync validation use case does not follow from the design
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer writes the fsync checker described in message #1 and registers a handler. The checkpointer calls it only for FileTags whose handler field holds its own ID, so md, CLOG and multixact requests never reach it. The tool reports no missing fsyncs because it never saw them.
refuted.argument: Dispatch is syncsw[tag.handler], so a handler sees only its own requests, yet message #1 says a validation extension will observe every sync request. Without that use case, the demand shown is one out-of-tree extension, Lamstore. The quoted Heikki and Andres wishes are about watching all files dirtied at the fd layer, which this API does not reach. So the second user does not yet exist.
refuted.author_must_show: How would a validation extension using register_sync_handler() see md and SLRU sync requests, and which users other than Lamstore need this API today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which states the same dispatch fact more narrowly.

refuted.title: Fixes a sync-side registration API before smgr extensibility is designed
refuted.failure_scenario: Core ships register_sync_handler() in v20 and Lamstore depends on it. A later smgr design picks hooks or ties sync handling to the smgr entry. Core then has to keep two registration paths, or break the extensions built on this one.
refuted.argument: Lamstore needs a custom storage manager, and core has no way to register one; [P5] was returned partly because hook versus registration was still open. Message #1 calls this patch orthogonal, but its only real consumer depends on that unsettled design. A committer would likely ask to settle the storage-side shape first, so that the sync API is shaped by it instead of shaping it. Committing this alone fixes one half of a two-part interface.
refuted.author_must_show: What does a custom storage manager need from sync.c that this API cannot change later, and why should it go in before the smgr registration design is agreed?

critic.reasoning: Same speculative scenario as prior-attempts-1. Commit 3eb77eba5a5, quoted in message #1, kept the sync table separate from smgr on purpose, and message #1 says Lamstore's storage manager already works on stock Postgres.

refuted.title: FileTag and handler lifecycle become a public contract with unclear rules
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release widens FileTag or changes how sync.c hashes it. Out-of-tree handlers that packed volume offsets into FileTag fields still compile but stop coalescing or match the wrong entries. Users notice only when a checkpoint slows down or skips an fsync.
refuted.argument: Today FileTag, SyncOps and the handler IDs are internal, so core can change them freely. After this patch, every change to sync.c must consider external handlers, and nothing fails loudly when one is missed. The docs also contradict themselves: they say IDs need not survive restarts because requests live only in memory, then warn that removing the extension may cause durability problems. The proposal does not say what the checkpointer does with an unknown handler ID.
refuted.author_must_show: Which FileTag and sync.c behaviours does core promise to keep stable for extensions, and what happens to a request whose handler ID is not registered?

critic.reasoning: FileTag and RegisterSyncRequest are already in the public storage/sync.h, and any extension API can change across major versions. The unknown handler ID point is covered by replication-ondisk-1.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fsync queue forgets requests on failure
precedents_retrieved.summary: Fix the checkpointer so that when an fsync of a relation segment fails during a checkpoint, the pending fsync request is kept for the next checkpoint instead of being dropped. The patch stops the pending-ops bitmapset from being lost when it is unlinked from the hashtable entry, merges unprocessed requests back on failure, and removes segments that succeeded as it goes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it as redundant with work in another thread (by Craig and Andres) that turns fsync I/O errors into PANICs and overhauls the request queue, because retrying fsync after a failure is useless on Linux. He noted that the other patch still left the retry path for errnos other than EIO and ENOSPC, but rejected this entry on the grounds that the issue would be resolved in that other thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Rejected, since this will have to be dealt with one way or another in
that other thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: speed up pg_rewind by using copy_file_range() and skipping some fsync
precedents_retrieved.summary: Two pg_rewind patches: one syncs only the files pg_rewind changed instead of the whole target data directory, and one uses copy_file_range() in place of read()+write() for local rewinds. He also asked to drop the copy_file_range_support flag, because one EXDEV failure would turn copy_file_range() off for all other tablespaces and mount points, and to fix double-counted progress on fallback. The fsync patch skips files such as configuration files included from postgresql.conf. The visible messages do not show a reply after his last review.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent is the same idea. The thread contains no reviewer reply about earlier attempts. Message #1 points to the earlier smgr_register review, and the message reports that review only by analogy.

No standards or compatibility objection holds. The patch adds no SQL, GUC, catalog object, dump state or psql surface, and the change of SYNC_HANDLER_NONE to -1 is flagged in message #2 and lands only in a major release. The open points are safety and design questions: unknown handler IDs, whether one handler can observe another's requests, and FileTag conventions. Other angles cover those.

The proposal adds no WAL records, catalogs or on-disk format, and sync requests are in memory only, so pg_upgrade and replication are not affected. The SYNC_HANDLER_NONE change targets a new major version, so the ABI break is acceptable there.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. register_sync_handler() is a C API callable only from _PG_init during shared_preload_libraries, which only a superuser or the server owner can set, and such code already runs with full server rights. No SQL surface, role, or view is added. Dispatch of sync requests with unknown handler IDs is a safety question for the design angle.

Hot-path cost is not a concern: the extra load happens once per checkpointer call, and only on the checkpointer. No committer has engaged in three CommitFests, which affects committability, not the verdict.

No core feature or extension does this today. syncsw[] is fixed, SYNC_HANDLER_MD only fsyncs md segment paths, and no checkpoint hook exists ([P15] was returned), so the only fallback is a synchronous fsync on every write, which cannot replace checkpoint-time sync at an acceptable cost. The patch extends the existing sync.c mechanism, following the custom rmgr pattern, rather than adding a second one.
Two demand objections; the API is small, so the main gap is evidence of users beyond Lamstore.
